subsystems.name: Heat source and plumbing
subsystems.role: circulates seawater through hot rock so it can pick up chemical energy.

subsystems.name: Vent fluid
subsystems.role: the reduced, metal-rich fluid that carries the chemical disequilibrium.

subsystems.name: Chemosynthetic microbes
subsystems.role: the primary producers: they oxidise the fluid's reduced chemicals and use the energy to fix carbon into biomass, with no sunlight involved.
parts: carbon-fixation enzymes (e.g. the reverse Krebs cycle)

subsystems.name: Vent fauna and symbiosis
subsystems.role: animals that farm the microbes internally or graze on them.
parts: tube worms with symbiotic bacteria in a trophosome

subsystems.name: Mineral chimneys
subsystems.role: precipitated sulphide structures that give the habitat its shape and surface area.

subsystems.name: Observation and sampling kit
subsystems.role: how the ecosystem is reached and measured — nothing here is accessible without it.
parts: manned submersibles and ROVs with manipulators

buildSteps.title: Open a pathway
buildSteps.detail: Seafloor spreading cracks the crust near a heat source, letting cold seawater seep kilometres down.

buildSteps.title: React with hot rock
buildSteps.detail: The water heats to hundreds of degrees, loses magnesium and sulphate, and gains metals, hydrogen sulphide, hydrogen and methane.

buildSteps.title: Vent the fluid
buildSteps.detail: The buoyant fluid rises and jets out of the seabed at up to roughly 400 °C, mixing with near-freezing seawater.

buildSteps.title: Build the chimneys
buildSteps.detail: Metal sulphides precipitate on contact with cold seawater, growing porous towers around the vent.

buildSteps.title: Create the gradient
buildSteps.detail: Reduced fluid sits next to oxygenated seawater, giving microbes a redox disequilibrium to harvest.

buildSteps.title: Establish primary production
buildSteps.detail: Chemolithoautotrophs oxidise the sulphide, hydrogen and methane and fix carbon, forming the base of the food web.

buildSteps.title: Colonise with animals
buildSteps.detail: Larvae arrive from other vent fields; tube worms and mussels host the microbes internally and the community develops.

buildSteps.title: Collapse and disperse
buildSteps.detail: Venting shifts or stops, the community dies, and larvae must find a new field within a generation — the habitat is patchy and short-lived.

prerequisites.why: vent fields sit 2–4 km down, far beyond scuba or surface sampling.
fluids change composition the moment they are brought to the surface, so they must be measured where they emerge.
many vent microbes die or change behaviour when depressurised, so they cannot yet be cultured routinely.
most of the microbes have never been grown, so their metabolism is read from their DNA instead.
they show that the carbon in the food web came from vent chemicals rather than from sinking sunlight-fed debris.

pathway.milestone: vent fields mapped along mid-ocean ridges and back-arc basins; chemosynthesis established as a sunlight-independent route to a biosphere
pathway.unlocks: a working model of where life can exist without a star, and a template for searching for it elsewhere.

pathway.milestone: better pressure-preserving sampling and cultivation of vent microbes and their enzymes
pathway.unlocks: biocatalysts that work at high temperature and pressure, and a clearer picture of the metabolic limits of life.

pathway.milestone: ocean-world missions that sample plumes and ices (Europa Clipper and JUICE)
pathway.unlocks: a test of whether the same redox chemistry operates under the ice of Europa and Enceladus.

pathway.milestone: in-situ life-detection instruments on ocean-world landers
pathway.unlocks: the first direct check for a second, independent origin of life.
